verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 2.18 'One zero weight' [V]: 'the 7-dimensional representation of G2 ... The Chevalley-Serre relations hold [V for A1, B2, B3, B4 and G2]. This gives the site a route to G2 that stays inside the game'; 2.18 'Out of reach of these two recipes: every other representation ... says plainly that the matrices need more than the game [D]'. The passage supports the finding's expected. Oracle: lie_games.orbit_plus_zero_matrices(cartan('G', 2), [1, 0]) has dimension 7 and chevalley_serre_ok True; golden orbit_plus_zero_representations[type=G2;highest_weight=1,0].dimension = 7
verdicts.evidence: Read SPEC 2.18 whole at 006f50d (SPEC copy in my scratch directory). The [D] mark sits only on the 'Out of reach' sentence, and its 'their' means the representations out of reach of both recipes. The 7 of G2 is reached by the second recipe, which is labelled [V]. Oracle on copies of reference/ taken from the gate commit (python3 -I): orbit_plus_zero_matrices(G2, [1,0]) gives dimension 7 and chevalley_serre_ok True. minuscule_matrices on G2 positions 0 and 1 gives dimension 6 and False. verify.py section 14 asserts 'single steps, with weight 2 on the steps leaving zero, satisfy Chevalley-Serre' for G2 [1,0]. Build at the gate: site/src/components/tools/t12/rep.ts:441-444 returns 'This board has no minuscule node; its representations need more than the game.' whenever the board has no minuscule node, and golden types.G2.minuscule_nodes = []. Phase: orbitPlusZeroMatrices is phase 7 (SPEC 5.4 row; 5.7 row; 9.1 row 7; 3 M8 beat 7 '(Phase 7)'). That governs whether the recipe exists, not whether a statement printed now is true. Records: build-plan/agents/P5-A2-t12-representation-builder.md line 140 prescribes this exact sentence as the plan's. DECISIONS.md '2026-10-24 P5-A2: the verdict and the explanation (F11)' records it with 'What the specification left open: the wording. Default used: the plan's.' That is not a section 10 default and not an owner's answer, and it stretches the [D] text past its 'their'. M8 beat 6 at the gate keeps the same sentence to the representations out of reach. reports/gate-G5.md (report commit 28fa75a; it names gate commit 006f50d) records nothing on this sentence. No merge report of an earlier P5 red-team round exists.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because the [D] permission covers only the representations out of reach of both recipes, and the 7 of G2 is not one of them; R2 fails because the finding reads 2.18 correctly; R3 fails because the one-zero-weight recipe being phase 7 does not make a sentence printed now true; R4 fails because the oracle (orbit_plus_zero_matrices on G2 [1,0], relations hold) sides with the finding; R5 fails because the plan's wording, logged as P5-A2, departs from the [D] text and is neither a section 10 default nor an owner's answer; R6 fails because there is no record. A mathematical statement presented as fact that is wrong is a blocker under RED-TEAM-COMMON 4.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 8.4 bullet 1 ('Define every term on first use ... (Appendix C is its seed)') and bullet 2 ('Use the site's words consistently ... Give the standard term once, in the Lie theory paragraph'); Appendix C row 'fundamental position e_i | ... | fundamental weight ω_i'. SPEC 4 T12 uses ω_i only in its description for the builder and fixes no reader-facing string that contains it. Its acceptance asks for 'the explanation that some number in the orbit is 2'. The passages support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: SPEC 8.4 carries no [D] and no qualifier. SPEC 4 T12 (lines 1191-1201) writes 'the orbit of ω_i' and 'The basis is the orbit of ω_i' as specification text, and SPEC 3 M8's beats use only 'positions'. The glossary at the gate (glossary.mdx:91-94) heads its entry 'fundamental position e_i' and puts ω_i in the Lie theory column. M8's own Lie theory paragraph (m8-lie-algebras.mdx:182) gives 'e_i is the fundamental weight ω_i'. Its captions b3 to b7 say 'the orbit of e1'. The b10 to b12 captions are lesson props from ownCaption = repCaption (rep.ts:929-940), which prints 'the orbit of ω4' and similar. A git grep of site/src at the gate finds ω outside T12 only in the Lie theory paragraphs of M0, M4, M7 and M8, in the glossary and in unverified.json. Records: DECISIONS.md 'P4-A6: words, terms and glossary links' (M7) says 'e_i in the body and \omega_i only in the Lie theory paragraph'. 'P5-A2: the verdict and the explanation (F11)' and 'P5-A3: four challenge tools' record the ω wording as the plan's ('What the specification left open: the wording'). That is a builder's or plan's choice, not [D], not D1 to D19 and not an owner's answer. The known-and-decided list of P5-LENS-INSTRUCTIONS does not mention ω. gate-G5.md section 11 does not mention it either. Ambiguity for the owner: 8.4 bullet 2's list of site words does not name 'fundamental position', and SPEC 4 T5 itself calls a chooser option 'a fundamental weight'. Whether 8.4 governs text built inside a tool is therefore not stated outright. On M8 the ω strings sit in the lesson's own caption props as well.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because 8.4 has no permitting clause and 4.0 [D] says nothing about terms; R2 fails because the finding reads 8.4 and Appendix C as written, and SPEC 4 T12's ω is builder-facing specification text, not a prescribed reader string (the ambiguity is noted for the owner); R3 fails because T12 and M8 are phase 5 at gate G5; R4 does not apply, since there is no mathematical dispute; R5 fails because the P5-A2 and P5-A3 wording entries are builder choices, not [D], section 10 or owner decisions, and they depart from 8.4; R6 fails because there is no earlier record.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 8.4 bullet 5 'Numbers that have a golden value are written with <G>, never typed.'; 7.3 'Every number in a lesson that has a golden value is written this way'; golden weyl_dimension[type=F4;highest_weight=0,0,0,1].dimension = 26 (a phase 3 key, SPEC 5.7 row 'weyl_dimension ... 3'). The passages support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Golden at 006f50d: the weyl_dimension records include {type F4, highest_weight [0,0,0,1], dimension 26} and {F4, [1,0,0,0], 52}. Oracle: lie_games.weyl_dimension(cartan('F', 4), [0, 0, 0, 1]) = 26. m8-lie-algebras.mdx:113 reads "Out of their reach are the {'26'}-dimensional representation of <Tex src=\"F_4\"/>, studied in <Cite k=\"vE\"/>". The same lesson prints the 7 of G2 (line 134) and the 248 of E8 (line 113) through <G>. DECISIONS.md '2026-10-24 P5-A3: numbers typed without a golden value (instruction 5.8)' lists 'the 26 of F4' under that heading, so it misclassifies a number the golden file holds. The owner-held item (P5 lens instructions, known and decided; gate-G5.md section 11) is 'the practice of keeping typed numbers in brace strings so that the numbers-in-prose report lists none'. That concerns where typed numbers without a golden value sit. It does not make a golden-valued number typable. The RT-08 lens's own exemption (section 6) covers numbers with no golden value only.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because 8.4 says 'never typed', with no exception; R2 fails because the sentence states the dimension of the F4 representation of highest weight (0,0,0,1), which is the golden value; R3 fails because weyl_dimension is a phase 3 key at gate G5; R4 fails because the oracle gives 26, which confirms that a golden value exists; R5 fails because the P5-A3 fragment wrongly calls the number non-golden and the owner-held brace-string practice does not cover golden values; R6 fails because there is no record of this number.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.3: <G> 'prints a value of golden_data.json ... Every number in a lesson that has a golden value is written this way, so prose cannot drift from the data.' No sentence permits a path from another record or another board. The passage supports the finding.
verdicts.evidence: Oracle: lie_games.string_through(cartan('A', 2), (2, 0), 0) = [(2,0),(0,1),(-2,2)]. verify.py section 14 checks this string but stores no golden key for it. Golden minuscule_representations[type=A2;node=2].weights_dynkin_labels = [[1,-1],[0,1],[-1,0]], so entry [1] = (0,1) is a weight of the node-2 representation, which does not hold (2,0). m8-lie-algebras.mdx:61 and the b1 caption (line 65, fmt(wt('A2', 2, 1))) print the middle of the node-1 string from that record, while STRING_TWO (line 30) is computed and unused. Line 113 says 'E8, F4 and G2 have no minuscule node: their Cartan matrices have determinant <G k="types.E8.det_cartan"/>'. Golden types.F4.det_cartan = 1 and types.G2.det_cartan = 1 are separate phase 2 golden values, and they are not tied to their own records. No DECISIONS.md entry names either path. The P5-A3 report lists them under goldenKeysUsed with no reason. Partial point: for part (a), 7.3's literal rule needs <G> only for numbers that have a golden value, and the string's middle has none. That part therefore rests on 7.3's purpose clause and on lens attack 13. Part (b) is a sentence about three golden values printed from one board's record, so the cause stands.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because 7.3 has no clause allowing another record's path; R2 holds only in part (part (a) has no golden value of its own), while part (b) states the golden determinants of F4 and G2 through E8's path, so the cause stands; R3 fails because all keys are phase 1 to 5 at G5; R4 does not apply, since the oracle agrees with the digits, which the finding does not dispute; R5 and R6 fail because there is no record. On severity the rubric is silent: the digits are right, so this is not a golden mismatch, and 8.4's literal 'written with <G>' is met. The lens's attack 13 rates it major.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 8.4 bullet 1: 'Define every term on first use and link later uses to a glossary entry (Appendix C is its seed)'; Appendix C rows 'population', 'mutate', 'fire'. The passage supports the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Glossary at the gate has dfn anchors population (glossary.mdx:43), mutate (:55) and fire (:61). M8 at the gate links numbers, node, position, fundamental-position, minuscule-node, board, city, root-population, roads and heap. It has no Term for fire, population or mutate. Its uses are 'Firing node i sends' (61), 'Firing node 1 exchanges them' (73), 'the firing move' (80), 'firing node k permutes' (106), and in the sidebar 'the population of a city changes when that city mutates' (143). None of these defines the term. SPEC 3: 'M6 to M9 can be read in any order after M5', so these are later uses of terms that M0 and M4 define, and 8.4 asks for links whether 'first use' is read per lesson or for the whole site. Records: DECISIONS.md 'P5-A3: words, terms and glossary links' sets its own rule ('a later use of each glossary term that a page uses twice or more', whole-word test). That is a builder's reading, not [D], section 10 or an owner's answer. Even under that rule the 4 or more inflected uses of fire go unlinked. 'P1-A8: glossary links' lists fire among the anchors later uses link to. No M5, M6 or M7 entry exempts fire. M5 is phase 3 and M6 and M7 are phase 4, so all are in scope at G5. A round 1 confirmed finding (round1-confirmed-B.json) on M0 and M1 terms (finite type, highest root, affine) has a different cause, and nothing records fire in M5 to M8.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because 8.4 has no 'may' and no threshold; R2 fails because either reading of 'first use' requires a definition or a link that M8 does not give; R3 fails because M5 to M8 are phases 3 to 5 at gate G5; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because the P5-A3 'twice or more' rule is a builder record, not a permitted default, and fire breaks it as well; R6 fails because the round 1 glossary finding concerns other terms in M0 and M1.
